\section{States and expectation values}\label{sec:states}
A density operator on $\C^2$ satisfies $\rho\succeq0$ and $\Tr\rho=1$.
The Hilbert--Schmidt inner product is $\inner{A}{B}=\Tr(A^\dagger B)$.
Consider the maximally mixed state and the Pauli matrix:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:matrices}
\rho=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \sigma_z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
\begin{theorem}[Vanishing expectation]\label{thm:expectation}
For the state in Eq.~\eqref{eq:matrices}, the expectation value of $\sigma_z$ is zero.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Using linearity of the trace,
\begin{align}\label{eq:expectation}
\Tr(\rho\sigma_z)&=\frac12\Tr(\sigma_z)\\
&=\frac12(1-1)=0.\nonumber
\end{align}
This proves the claim.
\end{proof}
Theorem~\ref{thm:expectation} and Eq.~\eqref{eq:expectation} demonstrate cross-references.
Standard background is given in Ref.~\cite{nielsen2000}.
